end.summary:
• Practised average speed = total distance ÷ total time; calculated 40 km/h for a round trip.
• Practised a = (v − u)/t using u = 25 m/s, v = 0, t = 5 s; wrote −5 but gave the unit incorrectly.
• Discussed that acceleration can be negative and opposite to the direction of motion during slowing down.
• The idea that acceleration only means speeding up was still present at the end; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: They also identified that braking can give a negative value and that acceleration may point opposite to the motion, but the mix-up that acceleration only means speeding up was not corrected by the end.
